author: researcher-experimental
title: Measurement preprocessing test: noise-isotropic (unscaled) PCA front end vs per-feature standardization for the log-k MLP
text: Per-feature standardization amplifies near-noise-floor features, mainly early-time readings at the outer sensors (indices 5 and 35). This raises the effective noise the MLP has to learn to ignore. If the raw features are left unscaled, the additive noise stays i.i.d. and isotropic. Projecting onto the leading 32 principal components then keeps the signal subspace and discards most noise energy. The same MLP on this representation should reach val rel_l2 below 0.9x that of the standardized-raw MLP (P-003). The gain should be largest for k1 and k4. This is a measurement-design question: how should the sensor time series be weighted before regression? Under i.i.d. Gaussian noise the noise-whitened metric is the raw Euclidean one. Standardization distorts that metric in favour of features with low marginal variance, and these are exactly the features with the lowest SNR. Unscaled PCA is the classical optimal linear denoiser for isotropic noise. The proposal differs from P-003 only in scaler and PCA, so the comparison is a controlled single-factor ablation. Features are raw noisy temperatures in the same units as sigma=1e-3, so the noise is isotropic in raw feature space. The harness applies PCA after the scaler. With scaler=none, PCA therefore acts on raw features. The torch_mlp's LayerNorm makes it insensitive to the overall scale of the PCA scores, which are not standardized. 32 components capture the signal manifold. The intrinsic dimension is 4, but the map is curved, so more linear components than 4 are needed. noise_scale is applied in raw units before scaling. With scaler=none both interpretations coincide, which removes the P-007 ambiguity for this arm. To isolate the scaler effect, add a 'standard scaler + pca 32' arm. Otherwise any difference cannot be assigned to noise isotropy as opposed to PCA itself.

If it is equal, preprocessing is not the bottleneck and remaining error is capacity- or information-limited. A CRB estimate would then separate those two cases.

text: The noise-free sensor histories lie near a smooth 4-D manifold. With scaler=none, the leading 24 PCs of the raw features are signal-dominated and the discarded directions are mostly noise. An RBF kernel ridge on these scores, with log target, should reach val rel_l2 < 0.06 and below P-004's standardized-PCA run at identical alpha and gamma_mult. Standardizing first lets noise-floor features rotate noise into the leading PCs. This is a nonparametric alternative to the MLP, structured as a single-factor ablation against P-004. If unscaled PCA with KRR matches the MLP, the inverse map is a smooth 4-D interpolation problem and the remaining effort should go to denoising rather than capacity. It pairs with the revised P-005 to form a 2x2 design: {MLP, KRR} x {standardized, noise-isotropic}. Raw features share units with sigma, so the noise is isotropic before PCA. PCA is applied after the scaler, so with scaler=none it acts on raw features. 3000 training points (6000 with aug) cover the 4-D box densely enough for the RBF interpolant. The gamma 'scale' heuristic, applied to unscaled PC scores, is dominated by PC1's variance. gamma_mult=1.0 is a reasonable starting point but may oversmooth along low-variance PCs. All splits come from the same simulator and noise model. Hold the bandwidth fixed in a normalized sense (for example a median-distance heuristic per configuration), or tune both arms by the same inner CV, so the scaler contrast is not confounded by a gamma heuristic that depends on the scaler.

author: researcher-experimental
title: Estimator-target alignment control: MSE on raw k (posterior-mean estimator) vs MSE on log k for the same MLP
text: rel_l2 is a squared-error metric in k-space. An MLP trained with MSE on untransformed k approximates the posterior mean E[k|data], which is the MMSE estimator under the uniform box prior. A log-target MLP approximates exp(E[log k|data]), which is biased low by about Var/2 wherever the posterior is wide. The predicted wide-posterior region is the outer segments and parameters near the bounds. The same architecture with target_transform='none' should therefore achieve val rel_l2 no worse than the log-target P-003, and should be at least 5% better on k1/k4 if those components are weakly identified. Every active MLP proposal uses log targets, so there is no control for the target transform. The critic notes that if outer-sensor signal is weak, posterior-mean shrinkage becomes the relevant lever. Raw-k MSE training gives that shrinkage directly, without a forward model. The test is a clean single-factor ablation against P-003. It can distinguish two explanations of residual error: a transform-induced estimator bias, versus an information limit that no transform fixes. rel_l2 is computed in original k units, as ||k_hat - k|| / ||k|| aggregated over val, so it rewards the conditional mean. The bounds [0.5, 2.0] span only a factor of 4, so raw-k targets are well-scaled and the network does not need log for numerical conditioning. Positivity is not at risk, because the posterior mean lies inside the convex box. Any rare boundary overshoot is negligible relative to the metric. The splits share a simulator and noise model. Recast it as an equivalence test: |Δ rel_l2| < 3% relative, with a 95% paired CI. Separately, the k1/k4 signed bias of the log model should be negative and larger in magnitude than that of the raw model.

A null result, with both targets within the CI, means components are tightly identified and transform bias is negligible.
data.if_fails: If log clearly wins, either the log reparametrisation improves learnability of the inverse map (P-007's claim), or the metric is not pure squared error in k. Either way, log targets become the default. If there is no difference, posteriors are narrow and the remaining error is an approximation or capacity issue rather than an estimator-choice issue, which points effort at preprocessing (revised P-005/P-006) or ensembling.

title: Surviving surrogate spec: learned forward net + per-feature-variance chi² refinement, encoder-calibrated anchor, paired hold-out gate (absorbs P-010)
text: An MLP forward surrogate (log k → standardised traces) trained on 2700 simulations reaches a hold-out per-feature residual RMS of rho ≤ 2·sigma, noise included. When it does, minimising a per-feature-weighted chi² plus an encoder-calibrated Gaussian anchor lowers hold-out and val rel_l2 by ≥10% relative to the same encoder with steps=0. If rho >> 2, the paired gate disables refinement and the refined and steps=0 runs coincide. This challenges the 'no forward model ⇒ pure inverse regression' framing. The 4→D forward map of a parabolic PDE is smooth and low-dimensional, so learning it is easier than learning the inverse. A per-sample data-consistency step can then remove the encoder's regression-to-the-mean bias, which is largest on the weakly informed outer segments. Calibrating both the noise model (per-feature v_j) and the prior (encoder hold-out RMSE) from data, rather than hand-tuning them, makes this an approximate MAP under a learned likelihood and a data-centred prior. Training features already contain sigma=1e-3 noise, so the hold-out residual variance is floored at sigma² and the ideal rho is ~1 Surrogate error is approximately independent across features with feature-specific variance v_j. Correlated structure is ignored, which is cheaper than full covariance and better than an isotropic weight The encoder error is roughly Gaussian per component with RMSE e_c, so a precision of 1/e_c² is a sensible anchor. Double-counting of data information is accepted as an approximation Adam with box projection in standardised log k converges within 200 steps near the encoder guess rel_l2 aggregation is unknown. The gate uses the global Frobenius ratio, and both common definitions rank methods similarly at this error level

title: critique r3 of Measurement preprocessing test: noise-isotropic (unscaled) PCA front end vs per-feature standardization for the log-k ML
text: Standardization is an invertible linear map. An MLP whose first layer is linear can in principle undo it, so standardization changes optimization and implicit regularization, not the information available. The 'noise amplification' story is therefore really about inductive bias. A ≥10% gain would need an optimization explanation, and the hypothesis should say so. The assumption that LayerNorm makes the MLP insensitive to the scale of unscaled PCA scores is unverified for the harness torch_mlp. If the first Linear layer sees PC1 with variance orders of magnitude larger than PC32, Adam may converge poorly before any LayerNorm acts. Verify the architecture or add per-score standardization after PCA. Standardizing PCA scores preserves the noise-isotropic subspace choice, which is the actual hypothesis. The k1/k4 sub-claim cuts against the proposal's own contradicting evidence. Unscaled PCA32 is more likely to truncate the small-amplitude outer-sensor directions than standardization is, so the predicted sign of the k1/k4 effect is genuinely uncertain. The rule estimate is 120 s, much above the self-estimate of 20–40 s, which strains a 400 s budget. A diagonal chi² treats it as independent, which overstates data information by up to the effective number of correlated features. Refinement can then lock onto surrogate bias, and the bias is largest exactly on weakly identified k1/k4. rho is an average and the gate keys on aggregate hold-out residual. Surrogate error concentrated near box corners or at extreme k values is where refinement matters most, and the average will not reveal it. The encoder is trained on 90% of the data, and the paired comparison is internal. That design is clean for the refinement question, but it gives no information about whether the final pipeline beats the full-data P-003. The rule-based 30 s understates two MLP trainings plus batched refinement. 60 s is more realistic. Surrogate residuals should be modelled with a low-rank covariance: project residuals onto the top-r PCs of the hold-out residual matrix and use a diagonal in that basis Stage 1 runs only if the encoder's hold-out rel_l2 exceeds 0.05. Otherwise refinement cannot be decisive. What is the effective rank of the hold-out surrogate residual matrix? A rank much smaller than d confirms the correlation concern. Is rho reported per k-region (corners vs centre)? The surrogate is consistently biased by +0.5σ along the direction where k4 enters. The chi² then confidently shifts k4 off-truth, and the refined error rises on k4 even though rho≈1.2. Use a residual PCA-whitened chi², or as the minimum, report the residual-covariance rank alongside rho. Add a stratified gate: report refined minus steps=0 error separately for k1/k4 and for k2/k3.
